findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the no-behaviour-change AC so each shard also passes `make lint` (and the type-check gate) unchanged, and add a rule that inline suppression pragmas (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and introspection-consumed doc bindings are treated as load-bearing (do_not_move), never relocated or collapsed on their own line.
evidence: The reconciler shard alone carries ~90 pragma comments whose removal is a lint failure, not a test failure: e.g. src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:50/63/75 `# noqa: F401` on re-export imports; applier.py:63-274 many `# noqa: E402`; _backend_registry.py:66 `import ... # noqa: F401 (side-effect: registers factories)`; binding_store.py:201/203 `# tickets-boundary-ok # noqa: E501`.

rebar_id_audit.py:62-66 pins `_AUTHORIZED_REBAR_ID_LABEL_WRITERS_DOC` with `# noqa: F841` and a comment stating the constant is read via getattr by a test — the exact 'architecture contract restated' shape the plan targets for ADR relocation.
None of the 8 ACs reference `make lint`, `ruff`, or a type-check gate; the only behaviour-guard is the test suite, which is blind to F401/E402/E501/F841 suppression removal.
findings.finding: The plan's only no-behaviour-change verification is 'the full test suite passes unchanged', but a large class of in-scope comments are lint/type-checker-load-bearing pragmas (`# noqa: F401` on side-effect/re-export imports, `# noqa: E402`, `# noqa: E501`, `# noqa: F841`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) that tests cannot observe — relocating or collapsing them breaks `make lint`, not the suite, so the mechanism does not detect the task's most likely silent failure.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (supersedes) — 'No behaviour change: the full test suite passes unchanged across every shard.'
scenarios: A shard collapses or relocates a `# noqa: F401` side-effect-import comment (e.g. adapters/__init__.py:15-16) as 'history/rationale'; imports register nothing or ruff re-flags F401; tests still pass green and the shard lands lint-broken.

The rebar_id_audit DOC block is relocated into a new ADR (it is a 4-8x-restated authorization contract, precisely the ADR candidate the plan describes); F841 fires and/or the getattr-reading contract test breaks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the superseded AC list: 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint`/type-check pass unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any doc string a test reads via introspection are load-bearing by definition — they go on every shard's do_not_move list.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to each of the five non-9ce8 shards an AC requiring the shard to measure (by diff line-count) and record on its ticket the actual comment lines recovered.
evidence: Parent AC: 'Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards.'
9ce8 alone carries: 'The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the unreliable ~970 estimate.'
4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c, ab77 each carry only four ACs: non-KEEP disposition, do_not_move-before-edit, verified-stale, and no-invariant-lost — none mentions measuring or recording a line count.
findings.finding: The parent AC requiring each shard to MEASURE and RECORD the actual recovered comment-line count on its own ticket is delivered by only one sibling (9ce8). The other five shards' acceptance criteria do not include a measure-and-record obligation.
scenarios: ad16 lands recovering 150 lines instead of ~230; with no measure-and-record AC the shard is marked complete without ever recording the figure, and the parent cannot compute the net total it is required to record.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c, and ab77 the same measure-and-record AC 9ce8 carries, framed as an output not a target.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c, and ab77 an AC requiring each shard's enumerated ADRs/amendments to exist and be committed before any citing comment is collapsed.
evidence: Parent AC: 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets ... EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that shard's own enumerated ADR set.'
9ce8 alone carries: 'Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed or deleted -- destination first, then the relocation.'

4b94 proposes a web-search ADR (capabilities.py:166-198); 4fc1 proposes 'Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation'; ad16 proposes three ADRs (attestation manifest, Burr tripwire, gate-context-never-elided); ab77 proposes three ADRs from review_bot/; yet none of these five shards' ACs mention ADR-before-collapse ordering.
findings.finding: The parent AC requiring every enumerated new ADR / amendment to EXIST AND BE COMMITTED before any citing comment is collapsed ('destination first, then relocation') is delivered by only one sibling (9ce8). The other five shards each propose new ADRs but carry no ADR-ordering AC.
scenarios: ad16 collapses the eight 'gate context is never elided' sites to 'see ADR NNNN' before that ADR is committed; the citation dangles and the withdrawn-alternative signed-false-PASS argument is lost, unrecoverable from the diff — exactly the failure mode the parent AC and the 9ce8 correction guard against.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy 9ce8's 'destination first, then relocation' ADR-ordering AC into the other five shard tickets, scoped to each shard's own enumerated ADR set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a 'no behaviour change: the relevant test suite passes unchanged' AC to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c, and ab77.
evidence: Parent AC: 'No behaviour change: the full test suite passes unchanged across every shard.'
9ce8 alone carries 'No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged.'
4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c, ab77 each list only four ACs, none referencing tests or behaviour change.

Several shards perform ->CODE fixes and field deletions with behavioural risk: 4b94 deletes the extra_tools field; 4fc1 extracts a helper in reads_cli.py; da4c relocates SNAPSHOT-restore migration-guard rationale; ab77 fixes a live BridgeFsckOut schema defect — these are not pure comment edits.
findings.finding: The parent AC 'No behaviour change: the full test suite passes unchanged across every shard' is covered by only one sibling. 9ce8 carries 'No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged'; the other five shards carry no test-passing / no-behaviour-change AC at all.
scenarios: 4b94 deletes the extra_tools field (a code change, not a comment change) and a test that referenced the field regresses; with no test-passing AC on the shard the change lands marked complete while the parent's no-behaviour-change AC is silently violated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 9ce8's no-behaviour-change AC (scoped to each shard's touched subtree, or the full suite) to the other five shard tickets.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC to each shard (or at least the shards that relocate history) requiring history citing a ticket to be reduced to that citation and history citing none to have a ticket filed before collapse.
evidence: Parent AC: 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first.'

No shard AC across the roster contains 'ticket filed first' or 'reduced to the citation' — each shard's four ACs cover only non-KEEP disposition, do_not_move ordering, verified-stale correction, and no-invariant-lost.
ad16 body (not an AC): 'Only two are costly: untracked follow-ups in production_batch_runner.py that must be filed first.'
findings.finding: The parent AC 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first' is covered by NO sibling's acceptance criteria. Two shards mention the behaviour in prose (4b94 'history already citing b690...'; ad16 'untracked follow-ups ... that must be filed first') but neither states it as an AC, and the other four shards are silent.
scenarios: A shard collapses a history block that cites no ticket down to nothing (deletion) without first filing a ticket; the historical rationale is lost with no citation destination, violating the parent AC while every shard AC still reads as met.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parent's history AC verbatim to each shard ticket that relocates history blocks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bind the 'no load-bearing invariant lost' criterion to a concrete check: every block on that shard's committed do_not_move list is still present verbatim in src after the shard lands.
evidence: 'No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim.'
The do_not_move list is described as 'the protection record' but this AC does not bind the check to it.
findings.finding: The criterion 'No load-bearing invariant is lost' states a subjective negative outcome whose only concrete verification hook is the narrower clause 'measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim'; the broader 'load-bearing invariant' judgement is not tied to a deterministic in-session check.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (supersedes) — 'No load-bearing invariant is lost' bullet
scenarios: A reviewer at PR time cannot deterministically confirm nothing load-bearing was dropped beyond the verbatim-string subset.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'No load-bearing invariant is lost — every entry on the shard's committed do_not_move list, plus all measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings, remains verbatim in src (grep-verifiable in the closing diff).'

findings.finding: AC3 requires 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035)' to exist before collapse, but this parent plan neither enumerates the ~13 new ADRs nor lists which shard owns which amendment, so the parent cannot self-verify the ADR-first ordering; verification is fully delegated to shard tickets that are not shown here.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign signing.py to a shard scope (its path determines which) so its comments are triaged and its security invariants recorded on a do_not_move list.
evidence: Parent body: 'comment triage cannot fix three files. _store/event_append.py (791) recovers ~10 lines; reducer/_processors.py (777) recovers ~3; signing.py (798) recovers ~5-8.'
da4c names only two of the three: 'this shard establishes that comment triage CANNOT fix the two size-pressured files here ... event_append.py ... _processors.py'.
No shard scope statement includes signing.py: 9ce8 = reconciler subtree; da4c = _store/reducer/graph/_snapshot; ab77 = root *.py + attest/metrics/review_bot/opcert_service/audit/grounding/_guides.
findings.finding: Owned-by-none scope gap: the parent explicitly names signing.py (798) as one of the three files comment triage cannot fix, but no shard in the roster owns it. The reconciler shard (9ce8) covers _engine/rebar_reconciler/**, store/reducer shard (da4c) covers _store/reducer/graph/_snapshot, and root/services (ab77) covers root *.py plus named service dirs — signing.py falls in none of the enumerated scopes, and da4c only names event_append.py and _processors.py as its two negative-result files.
scenarios: signing.py's ~5-8 recoverable lines and, more importantly, its security-invariant comments are never triaged nor entered on any shard's do_not_move list because no shard claims the file; a future sweep re-flags them.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm signing.py's path and extend the owning shard's scope statement to include it, or add it to da4c's negative-result set as the third file.

findings.finding: The plan's headline deliverable — recovering ~2,033 lines and restoring headroom on named hotspots (runner.py 3 → ~48, etc.) — has no covering acceptance criterion; all six ACs measure process (shards land, lists appended, ADRs written, stale comments corrected) rather than the line-recovery outcome the whole rationale rests on.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (all six) vs. body 'Total recoverable: ~2,033 lines' / 'Headroom recovered where it is tightest'
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Each shard reduces src comment lines by at least [per-shard target], verified by diff line-count; net recovery across shards ≥ ~2,000 lines.'

findings.finding: AC4 requires 'Proposed ADRs are written' but the plan only states '~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards' and enumerates a single example; the specific ADR set the executor must author is not listed, leaving the criterion unmeasurable and the scope undefined.
findings.location: AC4 'Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations' / body '~13 new ADRs are proposed'
findings.suggested_fix: List each proposed ADR title/subject in the plan (or reference the shard artifact that enumerates them) and change AC4 to 'Each ADR in [list] is written'.
